# Handling of the GPT round 2 review report

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Original report | `review/metis-review-vong-2.md` (GPT, 02/10/2026): conclusion Go with conditions; of the 54 round 1 proposals, 39 closed, 11 partly closed, 1 not closed, 3 with new defects introduced; 24 new proposals RF2-01 to RF2-24 |
| Applied to | BRD version 4.3 (`brd/`), wireframes (`wireframes/`, 45 screens), style guide 0.3 (`brand/`) |
| Constraint from the product owner | Keep assumption A-07 unchanged: an agency of about 40 developers, no cutting scope because of team size. The round 2 report complies with this constraint and proposes no scope cut |
| How it was handled | Each finding was checked against the real files before fixing. Every finding that could be checked was correct: the readiness on the workspace setup screen deviates from WSP-14; Program is made mandatory on the project creation screen; two different table row heights in the style guide; the personal token annotation on the AI access screen is outdated; the dashboards lack the metric version; §16 still has the words "any MCP-capable"; §1.7 lumps GOV-23 into the group of new requirements; the 1A milestone pulls in PLT-02, the portfolio read tool and the gate configuration, which are not there yet |

Result notation: **Applied**, **Partly** (applied with adjustments, or the remainder belongs to Discovery), **Not applied** (with a reason).

## Proposals RF2-01 to RF2-24

| Id | Proposal | Result | Reason and where it was fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| RF2-01 | Lock the foundation contract pack before opening the streams | Applied | §18.4: a "foundation contract pack" of nine items and a "walking skeleton" (a thin path through every contract) are the exit condition of Discovery; §18.2 adds working agreements between the streams |
| RF2-02 | ADR and a testable tenant isolation matrix | Partly | Added a draft isolation matrix right after the M02 table (each data path has one boundary and one negative test). The ADR and the test suite that really runs are item 1 of the foundation contract pack, which can be done only when D-28 is settled |
| RF2-03 | Fill in numbers for D-26 | Partly | §17.1 proposes starting values for every target; D-26 becomes a "confirm or adjust" decision. The final figures are still settled by the client with the pilot workload |
| RF2-04 | PLT-02 is pulled into 1A | Applied | §18.2: 1A includes M01 except PLT-02; 1B states client access (PLT-02) explicitly if D-02 approves |
| RF2-05 | The milestones of the MCP tools do not match | Applied | Rule: a read tool arrives with the module that holds its data. get_portfolio_summary moves to 1B; list_risks splits project risks (1A) from portfolio risks (1B); the decision-preparing tool of MCP-08 is in 1B; §18.2 and D-30 match the tool table |
| RF2-06 | Publishing a lifecycle in 1A depends on the gate configuration in 1B | Applied | The lifecycle configuration (stages, gates, mandatory artifacts, roles: GOV-01 to GOV-05) moves to 1A so that a framework can pass the check before publishing; gate operation (GOV-06, GOV-08, GOV-09, GOV-13 to GOV-15) is in 1B |
| RF2-07 | A machine-readable permission matrix | Partly | §14 and D-15 add a rule for combining permissions between the workspace and the project. The matrix file and the automatically generated permission tests are item 2 of the foundation contract pack, because D-15 is not yet settled |
| RF2-08 | Data retention values, sub-processors, legal matters | Partly | Item 9 of the foundation contract pack; the values depend on Q-11 and D-31; the legal side needs confirmation by jurisdiction [Unverified - confirm before applying] |
| RF2-09 | The pilot metrics have no targets yet | Applied | §18.5: a proposed target for each metric, a measurement window of the last four weeks of the pilot, the pilot sponsor together with the design partner as the person responsible, separate targets when the two partners have different baselines |
| RF2-10 | D-15 is not yet in the group of decisions to settle first | Applied | §19.1: the foundation group is D-28, D-20, D-03, D-15; before the architecture is settled: D-26, D-31; in parallel after that: D-24, D-29, D-09; D-02 before building the client access path |
| RF2-11 | §1.7 lumps GOV-23 into the new requirements | Applied | §1.7 separates them: 9 new requirements, while the existing GOV-23 now also records the owner |
| RF2-12 | §16 still says "any MCP-capable" | Applied | §16 states MCP-compliant clients within the tenant's client policy (MCP-20); a similar sentence on the sign-in screen is fixed |
| RF2-13 | Workspace setup readiness deviates from WSP-14 | Applied | `36-workspace-setup`: exactly the four WSP-14 rules; the steps follow the WSP-14 checklist; creating the first project becomes a step after activation |
| RF2-14 | Program is made mandatory | Applied | `37-project-create`: Program is marked "optional" and removed from the mandatory list and the annotation |
| RF2-15 | Undo is missing for writes through MCP | Applied | MCP-19 adds an Undo rule (who, when, how it is recorded, not touching the baseline); `42-editor-states` has an Undo button and an annotation |
| RF2-16 | The personal token annotation is outdated | Applied | `04-tenant-admin-ai-access`: the allowlist contains only OAuth clients; personal tokens are switched on or off per workspace; the client name of a token is marked "self-reported" |
| RF2-17 | Dashboards lack the metric version | Applied | The data as-of time comes with "metrics v1" in the cockpit, workspace dashboard, registry, capacity, risk, SteerCo, project overview |
| RF2-18 | The sign-in recovery states are missing | Applied | `43-access-states`: forgotten password, SSO error, expired invitation |
| RF2-19 | Bare V2/V3 labels | Applied | The "Planned V2/V3" label is written as real text in the HTML on every screen and the sidebar (the CSS no longer adds text by itself); two labels that were missed are fixed; the text version of the wireframes now reads the labels |
| RF2-20 | The scope of in-place help is unclear | Applied | PLT-20: a tooltip at the first appearance of each term on each screen; a help button and the terminology on the top bar of every screen |
| RF2-21 | The approval queue lacks deliverable approvals | Applied | `38-my-approvals`: added a row for approving an item, labeled Approval Gate, waiting at the review step |
| RF2-22 | MCP behavior has only tool names on the screens | Partly | Contract tests for each class of MCP tools are in item 8 of the foundation contract pack and in the §21 checklist; the risk "requirements and wireframes diverge" is added to §20. The tests themselves are written in Discovery and during the build |
| RF2-23 | Two different row heights | Applied | Style guide 0.3: tables 36px comfortable, 32px compact; lists 44px and 36px; a compact mode token; `tokens.css` records version 0.3 |
| RF2-24 | Dialog accessibility has no checklist | Applied | Style guide section 7a adds a checklist for dialogs and drawers; `42-editor-states` has an annotation about dialog focus |

## The seven questions for the client in part G

All seven questions were answered by the team with a recommendation in the BRD; the product owner may change them.

| Question | How it was handled |
|---|---|
| Under which rules is a workspace activated | WSP-14 is the authoritative source; the screen is fixed to follow WSP-14 (RF2-13) |
| Can a lifecycle in 1A be published while there is no gate configuration | The gate configuration moves to 1A (RF2-06) |
| Is the MCP tool that reads the portfolio in 1A | No; it arrives in 1B with its module (RF2-05) |
| Undo for writes through MCP | A rule in MCP-19 (RF2-15) |
| "At least two tenants" when there is only one design partner | §18.5: the second tenant may be a second customer or a pilot tenant operated by the provider |
| Tooltip at every appearance or only the first | The first time on each screen, plus the global terminology (RF2-20) |
| Who approves the pilot metric targets | The pilot sponsor together with each design partner; separate targets when baselines differ (RF2-09) |
